page: Amazon Web Services i3.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores with hyper-threading running at 2.3 GHz, backed by 488.0 GB of system memory. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 15,200 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. It operates on the Xen hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the older architecture of the Intel Xeon E5 v4 family. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth scale to average levels in the middle 50%. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as bzip3 decompression, also perform at average speeds when multi-threaded, though single-threaded operations remain weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i3.16xlarge offers high resource density, particularly regarding local NVMe storage and memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on older CPU architecture, which limits single-threaded compute efficiency compared to newer generations. However, for workloads requiring high-capacity, low-latency local storage without the need for cutting-edge single-core processing power, the hardware profile remains highly resource-dense.

This instance is designed for storage-intensive workloads. Appropriate use cases include large transactional databases, NoSQL databases, data warehousing, and high-throughput log processing where massive local NVMe storage and high memory capacity are critical.
